text:
emma-cs: Heads up — Ignite onboarding is blocked. Android app reports a flurry of 401s followed by 429s during SDK init. Customer sees ~300 devices booting in a short window.

sam-platform: Thanks — can you paste the top of the log around a failing session? Are they using ephemeral keys or a long-lived key? SDK version?

emma-cs: Using android-sdk 1.4.0, ephemeral tokens via our /token endpoint. Snippet:

```
I/System.out: POST /v1/generate 401 Authorization: missing
I/System.out: retrying auth -> fetch /token
I/System.out: POST /v1/generate 429 quota_exceeded window=60s
```

Many of the 401s are immediately followed by retries that hammer /v1/generate and then the 429s. They said connection pool size is default (8) but they spawn multiple worker threads at app start.

mohit-eng: This looks like a classic token stampede -> preflight fanout. If many clients call fetch-token then immediately call generate, you can get a burst where the first request authenticates but subsequent inflight requests still use the old/absent header. Two quick checks: (1) are they awaiting token fetch before calling SDK init? (2) are they reusing the same OkHttp connection across threads?

emma-cs: They call SDK.init() from several activities without awaiting the token promise. OkHttp is shared but some calls appear to race.

linda-support: We've seen this pattern with mobile fleets. Short remediation steps we give customers: reduce concurrent init, add small jitter before calling generate after token fetch, and enable client-side preflight coalescing in SDK. Example config (Android):

```
// pseudo-config for SDK.init
SDKConfig config = new SDKConfig.Builder()
  .setMaxConcurrentPreflight(4)
  .setPreflightCoalesce(true)
  .setTokenRefreshJitterMs(3000)
  .build();

RedwoodSdk.init(context, config);
```

Also recommend exponential backoff on 401 -> refresh -> replay once, not aggressive retries.

sam-platform: +1. For this customer I recommend server-side short-term workaround: return a cached ephemeral token for a few seconds to smooth the burst, or queue token issuance behind a tiny semaphore. Long-term: we should document the init pattern in mobile onboarding docs.

emma-cs: I can send them a quick patch to wait on token promise and drop concurrent inits. Do we have a snippet for OkHttp single-threaded init?

mohit-eng: Yep — simple pattern: single entrypoint for SDK.init guarded by an AtomicBoolean and a single-threaded executor for token refreshes. Also ensure Authorization header is added per-request rather than assumed present on pooled connections. Example:

```
AtomicBoolean initInProgress = new AtomicBoolean(false);
if (initInProgress.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
  executor.submit(() -> {
    String t = fetchToken();
    sdk.initializeWithToken(t);
    initInProgress.set(false);
  });
}
```

And use an Interceptor to inject the header on each call.

linda-support: I'll DM a short KB we can paste to the customer. Emma — if you want, cc me on the reply and I can include a one-pager about rate window behavior and suggested SDK flags.

emma-cs: Thanks — sending patch now. I'll add the jitter, set max concurrent preflight to 3, and advise them to upgrade to 1.4.1 (we patched a token race in that build). Will update here after they test. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [metric-alert] rate.window.ignite.prod spike -> 429s increased by 420% in the last 5m (nodes: edge-12, edge-14). Ping @sam-platform

sam-platform: Noted. I'll watch the metric dashboard and hold a short call if the spike persists. Good remediation plan.

emma-cs: Verified with customer — after changing to single init + jitter the 429s dropped to baseline. Closing for now, will file a short onboarding note.
